items.title: Powerless F1 drivers frustrated by Bahrain F1 software glitch
items.author: llm_nerd
items.summary: F1 drivers expressed frustration over a software glitch during the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, with Lando Norris calling the electronic glitches "horrible" and Fernando Alonso criticizing the "too much technology" in the series. Max Verstappen compared the chaos to a Lego go-kart race, while Haas driver Oliver Bearman described the throttle pedal malfunction as "scary." Sergio Pérez also criticized the software failure, describing it as "unacceptable" and noting the lack of power during the formation lap on a wet track. The incident highlighted the complex machinery of F1 and its potential PR issues.

items.title: Nearly 200 People Under Observation After Irkutsk Lab Worker Dies from Plague
items.author: ericmay
items.summary: Health authorities in Siberia’s Irkutsk region have placed nearly 200 people under medical observation after a laboratory worker died from plague. The woman, identified as Daria Sh., a 27- or 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk anti-plague institute, reportedly told medical staff that she had accidentally broken a test tube containing live bacteria while collecting samples for testing. The Shelekhov district hospital was placed under quarantine pending an assessment by a special commission. At least 197 people who may have had contact with her were reportedly placed under medical isolation, including more than 100 in hospital wards.

items.title: Quantitative Finance with OCaml
items.author: leonry
items.summary: The sources indicate that OCaml is a language that offers a unique combination of expressiveness, correctness, and performance for quantitative finance. It is used to build correct, performant, and maintainable financial systems by leveraging OCaml's type system to prevent financial programming errors at compile time. OCaml's pattern matching and immutable data help manage complexity and reduce side effects, while modules provide clear boundaries around different financial logic components. The language encourages thinking about all possible outcomes rather than just the happy path, which helps in building robust trading systems.

items.title: A tribute to one of the best games on the Atari 2600
items.author: plicerin
items.summary: According to the sources, one of the best games on the Atari 2600 is Pac-Man, which was the best-selling video game on the console, selling millions of copies. Another notable game is Space Invaders, which was the second best-selling Atari 2600 game and sold over 6 million copies. Warlords is also highlighted as a multi-player game that is still worth playing, designed for up to four people. Additionally, Pitfall is mentioned as one of the top games according to fans. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to which game is the best, but they do highlight several highly regarded titles.

items.title: The Tao of Backup
items.author: vntok
items.summary: The Tao of the Backup Catcher is a book that explores the lives of backup catchers in baseball, emphasizing their roles as necessary yet often overlooked players who provide experience for the "real prospects." It highlights the themes of sacrifice, humility, and acceptance, using the career of Erik Kratz as a central narrative. The book is praised for its reflection on the beauty of baseball and life, as noted by Jim Abbott and Jeff Passan. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to specific questions about the book's official website or contact details.

items.title: Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and get its disk space back
items.author: privacyisntdead
items.summary: To turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and reclaim disk space, you can disable Siri and its features individually by enabling Screen Time to block Siri, then going to System Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy, flipping the Content & Privacy toggle off, and changing Siri to Siri Classic. However, this may not immediately free up storage space. For macOS 26, you can disable Apple Intelligence by going to System Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri > Apple Intelligence and toggling it off. To reclaim more space on macOS 27, you can use macOS Recovery Terminal commands to delete hidden Apple Intelligence generative models and visual assets, but this requires booting into macOS Recovery.

items.title: Homa: The end of TCP for AI clusters [video]
items.author: signa11
items.summary: The sources indicate that John Ousterhout, a Stanford professor, discusses the evolving nature of AI networking workloads and why traditional protocols like TCP and RDMA are becoming bottlenecks in modern data center environments. The video titled "Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford" posted on YouTube on 2026-09-17, and summarized by Sean Weldon, highlights that AI workloads are shifting from large throughput-bound transfers to smaller latency-sensitive exchanges, which are poorly suited to legacy protocols. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to the question but suggest that datacenter operators may need to support heterogeneous transport strategies.

items.title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with AI [video]
items.author: simonjgreen
items.summary: To scale intent, quality, and artistry with AI, Katie Dill recommends improving your inputs by providing more specificity regarding your brand and unique interests through specific prompts. She emphasizes the importance of having a defined point of view and brand standards, as AI will likely provide a generic perspective without it. Dill advises being intentional and leveraging AI to raise the ceiling of creativity, not just to speed up existing processes. The sources also mention AI's role in real-time video inspection for production-line quality control, enhancing efficiency and product quality.

items.title: A map of every lighthouse
items.author: karakoram
items.summary: From mapped.earth, a map of every lighthouse on the planet is available, along with other charted lights like lighted buoys. The map is interactive, with each lighthouse sweeping out its actual arc and the reach of the beams true to scale. The map of lighthouses in North America from Mike Huff and Ryan Huff shows more than 600 lighthouses along the Atlantic coast, including those in Canada, the US, Mexico, the Bahamas, Cuba, Belize, and Honduras. The USAlights website provides a Lighthouse Locator Map to find lighthouses around the United States.

items.title: Show HN: AI search for every photo and every frame of video on macOS
items.author: allenleee
items.summary: SCM, a macOS tool by allenv0, enables AI search across every photo and every frame of video on macOS. The Show HN thread on Hacker News flagged the project last week and amassed 86 points with 47 comments, indicating meaningful early engagement from the AI practitioner community. The project is hosted on GitHub, and the reception on Hacker News suggests users are curious about on-device media search capabilities and privacy-preserving workflows.

items.title: Bill Draper has died
items.author: bookofjoe
items.summary: Bill Draper, a pioneering Silicon Valley investor, passed away on Sept. 8 at his home in Atherton, California, at the age of 98. His death was confirmed by his daughter Polly Draper and his son Tim Draper, a venture capitalist who founded Draper Associates. Draper began funding start-ups in the early 1960s, long before Silicon Valley was known for technology. He was co-founder with his father of the West Coast’s first venture-capital firm and was honored with a lifetime achievement award by the National Venture Capital Association.

items.title: Interview with Chicken Scheme Maintainer Sjamaan/Peter Bex
items.author: veqq
items.summary: Peter Bex is a CHICKEN Scheme maintainer and professional Clojure developer. He maintains the HTTP and URI implementations for CHICKEN, contributes to the numerical tower code, and keeps the in-core copy of the irregex library up-to-date. He enjoys deep diving into code to improve it and squash bugs. Bex is also the go-to guy for SQL questions in companies he has worked at. The CHICKEN community has an IRC channel on Libera where people are described as super nice and helpful. The default editor for CHICKEN Scheme is Emacs.

items.title: cp: -r or -R?
items.author: zdw
items.summary: The `cp -r` command in Linux is used to recursively copy directories and their contents. The `-r` flag tells the `cp` command to copy directories recursively, meaning it will copy not just the directory itself, but also all of its contents, including any subdirectories and the files within them. This command is a fundamental component of Unix-like operating systems, including Linux and macOS, and is known for its file and directory copying capabilities.

items.title: Emitting metadata early makes building/checking Rust up to twice as fast
items.author: knuckleheads
items.summary: According to the sources, emitting metadata early in the Rust compiler can make building and checking Rust up to twice as fast. This improvement is demonstrated in a Hacker News post and a GitHub project called headstart, which shows a 37% faster build time on 16 cores. The blog post from Mozilla also mentions efforts to push metadata creation even earlier in the compiler front-end to further increase speed-ups.

items.title: Former SR-71 engineer talks NASA's Blackbird revival program
items.author: rkagerer
items.summary: NASA has approached several former SR-71A staffers to assist in a secret effort to return a retired SR-71A Blackbird to flight, according to Aviation Week. Two former test engineers confirmed that they were offered jobs for this purpose. NASA has not confirmed the existence of this project. The agency has also withdrawn SR-71 Blackbird 844 from display, sparking speculation about its revival. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding the revival program's specifics or objectives.

items.title: The evolution of effective altruism
items.author: bazzmt
items.summary: Effective altruism is a 21st-century philosophical and social movement that advocates for impartially calculating benefits and prioritizing causes to provide the greatest good. The movement developed during the 2000s, and the name effective altruism was coined in 2011. Philosophers influential to the movement include Peter Singer, Toby Ord, and William MacAskill. The movement has roots in various philosophical theories and communities related to doing good and rationality, and it has much earlier philosophical influences. The effective altruism community began to crystallize between 2009 and 2012, with many central EA organizations being founded during this period. The rationality community, which shares an interest in clear and careful thinking and evidence-based reasoning, also overlaps with effective altruism. The Centre for Effective Altruism lists four principles that unite effective altruism: prioritization, impartial altruism, open truthseeking, and a collaborative spirit.

items.title: Declaring a bird extinct: The median wait is 36 years after the last sighting
items.author: Heidi_70
items.summary: According to Birds History, the median wait to declare a bird extinct is 36 years after the last confirmed sighting, with a mean of 47.5 years. The shortest time was three years for the dusky seaside sparrow, and the longest was 124 years for the Kauaʻi nukupuʻu. The IUCN Red List states that a species is considered extinct when there is no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died, but rediscoveries have occurred after long periods of no sightings. The Aldo Leopold Foundation notes the risk of the "Romeo Error," where species are declared extinct only to be rediscovered later, which can be detrimental to conservation efforts.
